candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes tall stature, long fingers, and hypermobility — features inconsistent with Weill-Marchesani syndrome (which presents with short stature and brachydactyly). While LTBP2 variants can cause Weill-Marchesani syndrome, the phenotype here and the reference diagnosis specifically identify juvenile-onset glaucoma as the primary diagnosis. C001 names a different LTBP2-associated syndrome with an incompatible phenotypic subtype and does not capture the glaucoma diagnosis that is the benchmark reference.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Weill-Marchesani syndrome is a distinct connective tissue disorder typically characterized by microspherophakia, short stature, and brachydactyly — the opposite phenotype of what is described here; the reference diagnosis is juvenile-onset glaucoma with compound heterozygous LTBP2 mutations

case_quality_flags: LTBP2 is associated with multiple phenotypes including Weill-Marchesani syndrome and primary congenital/juvenile glaucoma; the tall stature and marfanoid habitus here distinguish this from classic Weill-Marchesani, supporting the reference diagnosis of juvenile-onset glaucoma
